findings.title: A Skin's text names a color that the Skin does not give (Graphite on all 15 Directions; all four Skins of Graphite Precision; Vermilion seal)
findings.steps: Open #directions. (a) On the card "Graphite Precision" press the chips Berry, Gold, Forest, Ember in turn. (b) On "Unbleached and Indigo" press "Vermilion seal", then "Start from Unbleached and Indigo" and open #summary. (c) On "Control Room" and on "Ink and Seal" press "Graphite". Read the sentence under the chips and the --accent value in the card's picture. Files: packages/core/src/catalog/skins.ts lines 5-6, 38-47, 64-65; packages/core/test/catalog.test.ts lines 414-442.
findings.observed: (a) The card says "A rose red…", "A warm yellow-brown…", "A deep green…", "A red-orange…"; the picture stays black and white and the main color is #2d2327, #2a261e, #212923, #2d2422 (vividness about 0.015). (b) The card says "The orange-red of a seal stamped on a letter"; the main color and the button are #703324, a dark red-brown; the Summary then describes this same color as "close to “Dark purple”". (c) The card says "Almost no color: a near-black main color"; the main color is light silver #bcc5d1 on Control Room (and on Evening Formal, Marquee Deco, Vegas Modern, Sunlit Studio; #b5bfcb on Motel Neon and Mall Sunset) and mid gray #414853 to #6a727d on the eight light Directions. Cause: a Skin sets the hue only and keeps the Direction's vividness and lightness; no test compares a Skin's text with the color drawn.
findings.expected: A Skin's sentence is true of the color the card draws on every Direction that offers it, or the Direction does not offer that Skin. The code review of the same day graded the same kind of defect (CR5-02, a fade that ended in another color than its text named) as major.

findings.title: Records say that Skins cite research and are complete Catalog records; a Skin record has no source, no evidence grade, and no review date
findings.steps: Read packages/core/src/catalog/skins.ts lines 15-30 (the Skin record) and 44-47. Compare with PROGRESS.md line 77, PLAN.md line 143, and docs/knowledge/03-research-of-2026-11-14.md line 7. Read packages/core/src/catalog/overlays.ts lines 28-29.
findings.observed: PROGRESS.md line 77: "Three Directions … and two Skins (“Indigo dye”, “Vermilion seal”), each citing the research records it draws on." PLAN.md line 143: "a Step, Option, Direction, Skin, Overlay, … is a record with plain text, a source, an evidence grade, and a review date." A Skin record holds id, name, what, three hue values, an optional vividness, and the headline fill; nothing else. The only link to research is a code comment. No screen says where a Skin comes from. The same line 7 of the research overview says the Studio uses the 2026-11-14 research for "the source lines of the six Overlays"; every Overlay source line names kb-perception-cognition.json or kb-aesthetics-satisfaction.json, the two older files.
findings.expected: Either the Skin record carries sources, a grade, and a review date (and "Indigo dye" and "Vermilion seal" name the record "Traditional Japanese colour names have no single screen value"), or the three records say that a Skin is the builder's own composition with no source. The research overview should say that the Overlays rest on the older knowledge base.

findings.title: "Plain Label" does what its own cited research record lists as an anti-pattern, and the records say that no Direction copies a brand
findings.steps: Read packages/core/src/catalog/directions.ts line 5 and lines 673-690. Open docs/knowledge/kb-japanese-design.json, record "Emptiness as a container, and the plain-goods approach in retail" (fields antiPatterns, designMoves, caveats). Compute the Direction's colors (deriveTokens) or read them from its card.
findings.observed: The record's first anti-pattern: "Imitating a known retailer's label (its red-brown, its typeface, its kraft paper) and calling the result a principle." Its design move: "Copy no company's label colour…". Its caveat: a company's look is protected by trade-mark and trade-dress law, "the tool must stay with the general principle". The Direction is a near-white page (#fcf9f7) with plain letters, a black button, and "one dark red" (#7f1f29, a dark red-brown) for marks and links; its name is "Plain Label"; its "Best for" line reads "food, household goods, stationery, clothing basics", the range the record describes for that retailer. The Direction's "Watch for" text, D53 point 5, and directions.ts line 5 ("No Direction copies a brand") say nothing of this. The match with the retailer's real color rests on my memory, not on a source in the repository; the rest is the repository's own text.
findings.expected: The Direction either avoids the one color that its record warns against, or its "Watch for" text and D53 tell the owner that the look is close to a known retailer's and must not be used for a shop of that kind without a check.

findings.title: Four Overlays show guidance or a grade that is stronger than the record they cite
findings.steps: Open #overlays and open "Where this guidance comes from" on each Overlay. Compare packages/core/src/catalog/overlays.ts lines 49-109 with the records "Show progress during waits", "A wait feels shorter when it is explained, bounded and occupied", "Make actions reversible; forgive mistakes", "Errors: identify, explain, and allow recovery", "Always show what the system is doing and what just happened", "Fitts’s law and the steering law…".
findings.observed: Loading placeholder: shown as "long-standing convention"; its record says the evidence that such placeholders beat a spinner "is thin… That part of the claim has grade C", and the second record says "do not count on them to make the wait feel shorter". The figures "about a second" and "about ten seconds" come from a record that the Overlay does not cite ("Response-time limits: about 0.1, 1 and 10 seconds"). Main button that stays in view: "long-standing convention"; neither cited record speaks of a button that stays in view; "a large target that is always near is reached fastest" is the builder's inference, and the record's caveat says that on phones reach and the covering hand matter as much as size. “Are you sure?” question: the source gloss "undo is the stronger protection" is, in the record's words, "expert opinion, not part of a standard" and "a practitioner observation, not verified here", shown under "long-standing convention". Notice after an action: the risk sentence about a notice that vanishes has no support in the cited record, and that record advises confirming "where the user is looking (inline, or next to the control)", while the Overlay places the notice "at the edge of the window". PLAN.md line 57 promises that a rule graded C is shown as opinion.
findings.expected: "Expert opinion" for the loading placeholder and for the button that stays in view; a cited record for each figure; a gloss that keeps the record's own strength.

findings.title: Four research rules state their reason more firmly than their records do
findings.steps: Open #summary and open each research rule. Compare packages/core/src/catalog/researchRules.ts lines 75, 93-94, 110, 130 with the records "Line length: moderate lines, capped near 80 characters", "Short lines: reading speed holds until about 13 characters per line…", "A measurable floor for text size: lowercase letters about 8 CSS pixels tall", "Letter and line spacing…", "The smallest useful step between two sizes…". For the text-size rule, measure the height of the letter x in each offered letter style at 16 pixels.
findings.observed: Line length: "Studies of reading on screens favor moderate lines"; the record says the studies "are small and partly conflict" and that longer lines were read faster. "Reading stays fast down to about 13 letters per line"; the record says a reader at 13 "has already lost about a fifth of maximum speed". Text size: "16 pixels keeps the small letters above that size"; the record says 16-pixel text in a letter style with small letters "sits at this limit, not safely above it", with a floor of about 8 pixels give or take one. Measured in the Studio's own letter styles at 16 pixels: 7.9 (Source Serif 4) to 8.8 pixels. Step between sizes: "look like one size that was set carelessly… must be clearly larger"; the record says "risk" and calls the step its own inference (the rule's second text does say so). Line height: the upper limit 1.8 is the record's "working convention"; the screen gives no origin for it.
findings.expected: Each sentence carries its record's own limits: conflicting studies, a fifth of speed lost at 13 letters, 16 pixels at the limit and not above it, 1.8 as a working convention.

held:
Counted in the code and found as recorded: 23 Steps (6 Layout, 17 Look and feel); 38 Directions in four groups (12, 10, 11, 5); 13 Skins, each Direction offering 2 to 5; 6 Overlays; 5 research rules; 12 conflict and 11 harmony rules; 29 contrast pairs; project format version 2; 76 new research records (20, 20, 20, 16) and 138 older ones; 49 guarantees in version 1.4; 263 browser tests by count (104 in studio.e2e.ts, 159 in visual.e2e.ts: 10 single, 23 per Step, 9 per paint-only Step, 117 per Direction and page part), with 117 stored pictures; 19 code-review findings, 17 rows. I did not run the browser tests.

Test names: all 25 names in guarantees 10.14, 20.07, 30.06, 50.07, 50.08, 60.03, 60.04 exist word for word in the cited files, and each test checks what its rule says. All 35 names (31 distinct) in the saving table exist word for word, and its status-line words are in the code. All 12 test names and all commits in the findings rows exist.

Findings rows: CR5-01 to CR5-17, U2-06, U2-08, U3-05 are true at HEAD as written (CR5-11 measured at 44 pixels in a touch setting; U2-06 bar is opaque with one button; the notes and color chips of U2-08 are on screen).

Sources: every source line in researchRules.ts, overlays.ts, and the three new Directions (33 lines) names a record that its file holds word for word. The research overview's counts of how sources were seen match the data files.

Research rules against the drawn page (Ink and Seal, Plain Label, Control Room, at 375, 768, 1280, 1700 pixels): each "Holds" or "Does not hold" matches what the browser draws; text links are 24 to 26 pixels tall, as the rule says.

D52 and D53 otherwise: top bar reads "3. Overlays", "4. Summary"; a project without Overlays stores no Overlay field; an unknown Overlay planted in storage was left out with a notice and the original kept as a copy; no Overlay or rule is graded "measured"; four rules bind and Control Room departs; none of the 20 newest Directions starts with a contrast warning or a clash; no Skin adds a failing color pair (178 pairs computed).

Hard rules: no innerHTML or dangerouslySetInnerHTML in source; no React or browser API in packages/core (by search; I did not run the boundary tool); the Mockup holds no script and no event handler, in a frame with an empty sandbox; no outside request and no page error on any screen I walked; no text calls output "accessible" or "compliant".

Trial guide: every other label matches the screens. The branch name matches, and HEAD equals the local record of the pushed branch.

One slip of mine: a vitest run with the JSON reporter wrote /home/user/Frontend/.vitest/json/output.json. I removed it; `git status` shows no change.
